title.narrative: Output 1.3. Increased institutional capacity and resilience of labour administrations

description.narrative:
Improved institutional capacity of the State Labour Inspectorate (SLI) to address the increased risks of labour exploitation and trafficking in persons for Ukrainians being forced to leave their homes because of Russia’s armed conflict with Ukraine. The campaign consisted of information materials, a hotline, as well as physical outreach of labour inspectors to refugees/internally displaced persons at major transportation points. Over 4 million persons were reached by the SLI campaign.
The ILO assisted the State Labour Inspectorate in the development and production of the outreach tools for its campaign on labour exploitation.

Output 1.4. Increased capacity of Member States to improve social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative: The ability of the Ministry of Labour to drive the labour law reform has been strengthened through the provision of a memorandum of technical comments of the draft law of labour of Ukraine. For example, the ministry was given policy options to align the law with ILS and comparative practices. The Office has provided an analysis of the draft law of labour based on international standards and comparative practices in February 2023. The Office has encouraged the Government to share the document with social partners to ensure that the process is based on social dialogue.
